content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I have several programs created in older [product_name] versions, and I'm unable to simulate them with [product_name] [version_no], even after updating the device in [product_name] [version_no]. I avoid saving them in the newer [version_no], as this prevents use on devices with an earlier [version_no]. It seems there isn’t a solution for this currently. Thanks in advance.
Could you upload one of your previous programs?
Here’s the file. If you have any questions, let me know.
For me, simulation works when the hardware is set to [product_name] [version_no].

This is where the issue occurs—I can’t perform an online test if the selected device is an older [version_no], even though the physical hardware is actually a newer [version_no]. In the program, I’ve selected the older version. I’ve included a screen recording (the error isn’t displayed) and a screenshot. I’ve had problems where the program can't be reused on an older device. [url]

Apologies, I’m unable to read or communicate in Spanish, so I can only guess the details. Your program appears to target [product_name] [version_no] hardware. With this setting, you can’t run online tests on actual [product_name] [version_no] hardware; it's not supported. If you want to run such a test on newer hardware, you’ll need to update the hardware setting in your program to match the newer [version_no].

I believe you are mistaken. A key feature of [product_name] is its up and downwards compatibility. In [product_name] [version_no], you can select an older hardware version and save your program. The saved program is then usable with any [product_name] version from [version_no] onwards. Additionally, you can have multiple [product_name] versions installed on your computer, or run [product_name] directly from a copy of the installation media without needing to install it. Hope this clarifies.
What about [product_name] Service Pack? The latest [version_no]? I always download from [company_name]'s website and haven’t had any issues working with them.
I think they were referring to an Update or Upgrade Service Pack.
I checked it two days ago. Anyway, I can’t check again right now, but tonight I will. Thanks.
Sorry, I’m having trouble understanding exactly what you mean.
I’m working at the moment, but I’ll explain more in detail later.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are running into limitations when trying to simulate or execute online tests in [product_name] [version_no] with projects from earlier [product_name] versions, specifically when the selected hardware version differs. There is confusion about compatibility and how different software and hardware versions affect the ability to use and transfer programs. Language differences and ambiguity in compatibility features add to users’ uncertainty.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to provide fully seamless compatibility between hardware and software versions, allowing simulations and online tests without having to convert file formats or risk losing backward compatibility.
